why:
The one thing #474 is about, run end to end: `due` names an expired catalog source as owed, and this is the tool that discharges it. `due.rs`'s own table says one of its four clocks is dischargeable by a tool at all — the index clock wants a build, and questions and phases want a person — so a server that drafts nothing here has the write tier and nothing reachable through it.

`dry_run: true`, deliberately. A case that wrote a branch would make every later case on this corpus run against a repository the earlier one changed, and on a second run against a persistent checkout it would meet its own branch and refuse. What is being conformed to is what the tool DRAFTS, and the draft is identical either way — `written` is the only field that differs.

The count is exactly one and that is the assertion worth making. A server that drafted two has found something in this corpus that the reference server does not license; a server that drafted zero has the tool and not the rule. The verb is `open` and not `establish`: opening a question asserts nothing the work did not already assert, which is why RFC-0020 licenses one and not the other, and a server drafting `establish:` here has proposed a synthesis nobody authored.
